mechanism_narrative: A higher federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) reflects restrictive monetary policy that increases corporate borrowing costs and reduces equity valuation multiples, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds the 75th percentile of its 10-year historical range, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 4.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates broad demand weakness that triggers equity sell-offs, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline from prior month levels, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial contraction regimes (INDPRO below 110.0), manufacturing output decline signals reduced corporate capacity utilization and lower earnings growth, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is below 110.0 during industrial contraction regimes, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% indicates persistent inflation that triggers Federal Reserve tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust labor market conditions that support consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS is above the 75th percentile of its 10-year historical range, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (as indicated by high residential construction), a slowdown in housing starts (HOUST below 1500.0) signals impending demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST is below 1500.0 during late-cycle expansions, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and payroll growth slowdown (PAYEMS growth rate below 0.5%) indicates broad economic weakening that reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both INDPRO and PAYEMS decline from prior month levels, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.
